lines.1: Speak of the devil--the Student Council President.
lines.8: 「Princess, you're giving the president's address today. Should you really be arriving this late?」
lines.11: 「She may not look it, but she's considerate.」
lines.12: 「She's easy to talk to, and she's funny.」
lines.15: 「But she never brags about it, does she?」
lines.16: For better or worse, merely passing by is enough to make her the topic of conversation.
lines.17: When we neared the school gate, she casually lifted her mountain bike.
lines.18: 「Is riding a folding mountain bike to school the latest rich-kid trend?」
lines.20: As demonstrated by the mountain bike currently slung over her shoulder.
lines.21: 「Still, doesn't she seem like a prime kidnapping target?」
lines.22: 「No idiot's going to pick a fight with the US military.」
lines.23: 「They've even got a supercarrier docked here.」
lines.24: The Princess is half Japanese and half American. Apparently, she lives on the US military base and commutes from there.
lines.25: We passed through the school gates.
lines.28: Whenever I pass through here, I always feel someone watching me.
lines.29: 「Our school's trial program for recycling paper cartons has raised our standing, with approximately two yen per kilogram donated to an international welfare organization.」
lines.30: 「All seven schools in the surrounding area have endorsed our vision and begun their own recycling programs. Matsukasa City has also featured these efforts on television--」
lines.31: I couldn't help being captivated by the sight of her onstage.
lines.32: Her clear voice carried through the vast gymnasium.
lines.33: 「--Going forward, we will continue our daily efforts, proud of our contribution to society and determined to set a good example for other schools. I ask for everyone's cooperation.」
lines.34: 「She usually does nothing but screw around, but the Princess always nails stuff like this.」
lines.35: 「That concludes my report. Erika Kiriya, Student Council President of Ryuumeikan Academy.」
lines.38: She's the girl I admire as a woman, and she's immensely popular at school.
lines.39: Popular, yes, but just as many people hate her, so calling her an 'idol' might be a stretch.
lines.40: Her personality is intense in every sense of the word, so everyone calls her 'Princess' with equal parts respect and sarcasm.
lines.41: The fact that no one has ever seen the Princess's skirt flip up is one of the school's seven mysteries.
lines.42: 「Aaaand next, we have a few words of guidance from our principal, Heizou Tachibanaaa.」
lines.44: Anyone who made noise now was either an idiot or suicidal.
lines.45: The principal appeared without a sound.
lines.46: They call our principal a dragon born too late for his age.
lines.47: 「Boys, hone your manly spirit! Girls, hone your womanly spirit! Revel in your youth!」
lines.49: The principal is popular because his speeches end in an instant.
lines.50: 「Heh heh. The principal's words always hit you right in the chest... That's our principal.」
lines.51: 「Yeah. Makes you want to give it your all for another week--really puts some fire into a competition.」
lines.52: The athletic types seem to draw encouragement from his words...
lines.54: The moment assembly ended, I started getting sleepy.
lines.55: 「That was a huge yawn. How undignified.」
lines.58: 「Watching someone with so little energy is annoying. I kind of wish you'd disappear.」
lines.59: She says some vicious things with a smile.
lines.61: 「Here, have a rose. Let its fragrance wake you up.」
lines.62: She handed me a rose she'd produced from nowhere.
lines.63: 「Y-you've still got some strange tricks up your sleeve.」
lines.64: 「A young lady's little accomplishment. If you strike a pose, you should at least be able to produce a rose.」
lines.65: 「By the way, Tsushima, your face is getting redder by the second.」
lines.68: ...Please don't stare at me with those striking, foreign features.
lines.70: She knows I'm flustered and she's teasing me for it.
lines.71: 「Well, I'd feel bad bullying you too much this early in the morning, so I'll let you off here.」
lines.72: The Princess smiled in satisfaction at my discomfort, then strode away.
lines.74: That's where I stand with the Princess.
lines.75: In other words, we're just classmates. Sometimes she talks to me, and when she does, she teases me.
lines.76: Maybe she doesn't take me seriously. Maybe she looks down on me.
lines.77: Then again, I was happy she spoke to me just now.
lines.79: That's what it means to have a weakness for someone, I suppose.
lines.80: I can talk normally with any other girl.
lines.81: But the Princess is the one girl who makes me nervous.
lines.84: Crab had watched the whole thing and was smirking at me.
lines.85: ...I'll make her cry for that later.
lines.87: We returned to classroom 2-C, and I took my usual seat by the window.
